data.description:
TB-32 bounded every agentsview subprocess call at AGENTSVIEW_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0s. The value is a module constant with no operator override.

60s is a compromise, and a compromise is wrong for somebody at both ends:

  - a large or slow archive can exceed 60s on a legitimate call, so a HEALTHY daemon gets
    killed and its sessions land under the export_timeout skip reason -- a truncated corpus
    caused by our own default;
  - an operator who knows their daemon is merely slow has no way to say 'wait longer', and
    one debugging a hang has no way to say 'give up sooner'.

ADD: --agentsview-timeout SECONDS on toolbench.passive.

  > 0   bound at that many seconds (default 60.0 -- current behaviour unchanged)
  = 0   unbounded: pass timeout=None, restoring pre-TB-32 blocking, deliberately
  < 0   rejected by argparse

WIRING: main() already takes an injectable runner defaulting to None, and BOTH consumers
(iter_sessions, and AgentsViewLoader via pick_adapter) independently fall back to
_run_agentsview. So main() builds the runner once as
functools.partial(_run_agentsview, timeout=args.agentsview_timeout). partial still satisfies
Runner = Callable[[list[str]], CompletedProcess[str]], so every injected test fake keeps
working and the flag reaches all four call sites with no new plumbing. _run_agentsview's
timeout widens to float | None.

DISCLOSURE (the part that is not merely a knob): the Summary names the timeout when, and only
when, it changed what the reader is looking at --

  - the run produced >= 1 export_timeout skip: a short timeout that truncated the corpus is
    exactly the 'report claims a population it did not scan' failure TB-21/TB-33 exist to
    prevent, and the reader must not attribute that gap to the archive;
  - the run was unbounded (0): otherwise a reader cannot distinguish 'AgentsView was healthy'
    from 'we got lucky', and the run could have blocked indefinitely.

A clean bounded run says nothing. No stderr warning in any case -- a Summary fact, not a nag.

Follow-up to TB-32 (PR #57), which named this flag as explicitly out of scope. Branched from
the TB-32 branch, not main: the constant this flag overrides does not exist on main yet.
data.title: AGENTSVIEW_TIMEOUT_S is a hardcoded constant: an operator whose daemon is legitimately slow, or legitimately hung, has no way to say so
